chunks: As for whatever is in it from ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām, I have narrated it from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may Allah be pleased with him—from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, who said: ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated to me.
And the name of Abī al-Miqdām is Thābit ibn Hurmuz al-Ḥaddād.

key_terms.الصَّفَّارِ: A well-known transmitter in the sanad/isnad.
key_terms.الْحَكَمِ ابْنِ مِسْكِينٍ: A transmitter in the chain linking the report.
key_terms.ثَابِتُ بْنُ هُرْمُزَ الْحَدَّادُ: The personal name and appellation of Abī al-Miqdām.
key_terms.عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي الْمِقْدَامِ: A narrator whose transmission path is being clarified here.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām. It also identifies Abū al-Miqdām by his personal name, Thābit ibn Hurmuz al-Ḥaddād, which is useful for hadith identification and narrator verification.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah (swt) be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Al-Hakam ibn Maskeen, who said: Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam narrated to me,
and the name of Abi Al-Miqdam is Thabit ibn Hurmaz Al-Haddad.
